title: Landing readiness check
description: Before landing, merge checks review stage, close-out evidence, lane identity, claim, dirty files, blocking QA, post-deploy QA and landing-route gates. The read-only --check uses the same checks. An item one declared edge before review is moved into review by the merge, running that stage's gates; --check asks the stage's database-claim prose gate read-only and reports a prose-vs-claim mismatch as a blocker, and its merge_will note names the stage's other gates, which only the merge's own transition evaluates. The run writer observes the start commit when available; the latest completed pass on an effective item requirement counts without commit comparison. Newer failures or incomplete runs, changed configuration or target, missing subject proof and human review still block. Required merge-queue CI tests the final commit. Source-observed; not yet verified-live. Missing-proof refusals name the requested action: merge checks say merge, while lifecycle checks name the transition and target status. Steering report landing reads make one GitHub transport attempt without retry backoff; a failed read stays unreadable for that report and the next report reads again. Other landing callers retain their retry policy. Red required-check readbacks list each failed check and URL once, followed by recovery guidance; the merge entry refusal keeps its complete diagnosis. Landing readiness reads auto-merge, the PR queue entry and required checks in one GraphQL projection per distinct PR. An enqueued PR remains in flight after GitHub consumes auto-merge; a failed PR read leaves the queue entry unreadable. Fleet reports never read the branch queue for landing readiness.
